AARON EDWARD HOWTON'S PLEADING IN RESPONSE TO ORDER REMANDING PROCEEDING TO SOAH
AND REQUEST THAT FINDINGS ON PRELIMINARY ORDER ISSUES 11 AND 13 STATE THE STANDARD, STUDY, DATA, AND ANALYSIS RELIED UPON
TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRATIVE LAW JUDGES: Aaron Edward Howton, Intervenor, files this pleading in response to the Commission's Order Remanding Proceeding to SOAH (Item No. 6578). This submission is confined to Preliminary Order Issues 11 and 13, the only matters remanded by the Commission. Mr. Howton does not request that SOAH reopen the evidentiary record, retry routing issues, or enlarge the scope of the remand. Rather, he asks that the ALJs' recommendations on Issues 11 and 13 be tied, finding by finding, to specific record evidence, so that each answer can be traced to the standard, the study, the data, and the analysis that support it.
I. THE REMANDED QUESTIONS AND WHAT A RESPONSIVE FINDING REQUIRES
The Commission remanded two questions. Issue 11: "Are the proposed transmission facilities necessary to meet state or federal reliability standards?" Issue 13: "What is the estimated congestion cost savings for consumers that may result from the proposed transmission facilities considering both current and future expected congestion levels and the ability of the proposed transmission facilities to reduce those congestion levels?" Order Remanding Proceeding to SOAH at 2-3 (Item No. 6578).
The Chairman's memorandum proposing remand explains what a responsive answer requires. On Issue 11, it states that the question is whether the facilities "are in fact necessary to meet state or federal reliability standards, not how the applicants characterize the project," and that the ALJs "should address the specific North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) reliability standards at issue." On Issue 13, it states: "If the ALJs find that the transmission line fails to establish need as a reliability project, the question remains of whether need was demonstrated as an economic project." Chairman Thomas Gleeson Memorandum at 2-3 (Sept. 9, 2026) (Item No. 6514).
Commission Rule 22.263(a)(3) requires the Commission's final order, when a finding of fact is stated in statutory language, to include a concise and explicit statement of the underlying facts supporting that finding. Issue 11 uses the reliability-standard formulation reflected in PURA § 37.056(d) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(A)(ii). A supplemental proposal for decision that supplies only the statutory conclusion would leave the Commission without the underlying findings its final order requires. Mr. Howton therefore asks the ALJs to state the record facts supporting the answer, not merely repeat the label.
II. ISSUE 11: A RELIABILITY FINDING SHOULD BE TRACEABLE TO A SPECIFIC STANDARD, A SPECIFIC STUDY RESULT, AND THE DATA BEHIND IT
Applicants classify Import Path 2 as a reliability project. App. Reply Br. at 24 (June 26, 2026). A reliability project is "a transmission line that is necessary to meet state or federal reliability standards." 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(A)(ii) (as quoted in Item No. 6514 at 2). That classification is what exempts the project from the congestion cost savings test. It therefore must rest on findings supported by record evidence, not on the label.
Mr. Howton does not ask the ALJs to revisit the Commission's approval of the Permian Basin Reliability Plan or to disregard ERCOT's studies. PURA § 37.056(c-1) directs the Commission, in considering need, to consider forecasted load growth "as determined by the electric utility with the responsibility for serving the load." The point here is narrower. Issue 11 asks whether these facilities are necessary to meet a reliability standard. That question is answered by the standard, the study result, and the data that produced it.
Mr. Howton therefore asks that the supplemental proposal for decision answer Issue 11 by stating, with a record citation for each, the following:
A. THE STANDARD
Each specific NERC reliability standard, by number and requirement, and each ERCOT planning criterion that Import Path 2 is asserted to be necessary to meet. The PFD refers to "NERC contingencies" in Finding of Fact 130 but does not identify the standard. Item No. 6514 at 2.
B. THE VIOLATION
Each study case, study year, contingency, and thermal, voltage, or stability violation that the record shows would occur without Import Path 2, identified for Import Path 2 specifically rather than for the Permian Basin Reliability Plan as a whole.
C. THE DATA THAT PRODUCE THE VIOLATION
The load and generation assumptions in each study case that produced each violation, and whether the record shows that the violation persists under ERCOT's later-adjusted load-forecasting methodology, which the PFD describes as reducing officer-letter-confirmed load. PFD at 63-65.
D. THE MECHANISM
Record evidence that Import Path 2 resolves each violation, including the generation expected to flow on it. The PFD found that Applicants did not identify specific generation resources expected to import power into the Permian Basin via Import Path 2, and that Applicants admitted no determination was made whether central Texas generation could serve local load and export power westward at the line's design capacity. PFD at 84-87; Howton Ex. JAH-32 at 15-17 (Applicants' Resp. to Howton RFI Set 4, Nos. 1-96 to 1-98).
E. THE TIMING
The first study year in which each violation occurs. The PFD concluded that the record does not establish that Import Path 2 is needed in 2030. PFD at 87-90.
F. THE ANALYSIS BEHIND THE CONCLUSION
Whether the record contains the underlying study work, meaning the power-flow cases, contingency lists, and results, or only a summary or conclusion of that work; and whether any party other than ERCOT and Applicants, including Commission Staff, reviewed the underlying work.
G. THE FEDERAL-LAW CONSEQUENCE
As the Chairman's memorandum asks, whether failing to build Import Path 2 would itself place any registered entity out of compliance with the identified NERC standard, and on what record basis. Item No. 6514 at 2.
The seven subjects above are not offered as a new legal test. They identify the record facts needed to show what reliability standard is implicated, what modeled condition violates it, and how Import Path 2 cures that condition. Where the existing record does not supply one of those factual links, the supplemental proposal for decision should say so plainly rather than bridge the gap by inference from the project's classification. PURA § 37.056(a) permits the Commission to grant a certificate only if it finds the certificate necessary.
III. ISSUE 13: THE CONGESTION FINDING SHOULD REPORT WHAT THE RECORD CONTAINS
Issue 13 tracks PURA § 37.056(d). For a project "not necessary to meet state or federal reliability standards," that subsection requires criteria that "must include a comparison of the estimated cost of the transmission project for consumers and the estimated congestion cost savings for consumers that may result from the transmission project," considering current and future expected congestion levels, and it requires the Commission to "include with its decision on an application for a certificate to which this subsection applies findings on the criteria."
Issues 11 and 13 therefore work together. If the ALJs find on the existing record that the proposed facilities are necessary to meet state or federal reliability standards, the economic comparison in PURA § 37.056(d) does not apply. If the ALJs do not make that finding, the Chairman's memorandum states that "the question remains of whether need was demonstrated as an economic project," and Issue 13 requires an answer regarding the estimated congestion cost savings for consumers. Item No. 6514 at 3.
The PFD found that "the record contains no evidence quantifying" the congestion cost savings. PFD at 150. The PFD likewise found that Applicants submitted a projected construction cost, not the estimated cost of the facilities to consumers. PFD at 149. Mr. Howton asks that the supplemental proposal for decision carry those findings forward as the answer to Issue 13: the estimated congestion cost savings for consumers is not established in the record, and the comparison PURA § 37.056(d) requires cannot be made on it.
If any party identifies a congestion-savings figure on remand, the supplemental proposal for decision should identify the figure's record source, the study that produced it, the current and future congestion levels and study years assumed, and the evidence supporting those assumptions. A number untethered to an admitted record source and the congestion assumptions that produced it should not be treated as the answer to Issue 13. If SOAH admits new evidence on remand, Mr. Howton requests a fair opportunity for discovery and cross-examination concerning that evidence.
IV. REQUEST FOR ACTION ON REMAND
Mr. Howton respectfully requests that the ALJs, in carrying out the Commission's remand: (1) address Issues 11 and 13 on the existing record, as 16 TAC § 22.262(c)(1) permits; (2) authorize the parties under 16 TAC § 22.261(c) to submit proposed findings of fact on Issues 11 and 13, each with a pinpoint record citation; and (3) state the underlying record facts supporting each recommendation framed in statutory language so that the Commission can enter a final order consistent with 16 TAC § 22.263(a)(3).
Mr. Howton further requests that the resulting findings distinguish among: (1) a study result accompanied in the record by the data and analysis that produced it; (2) a summary or conclusion of that result; and (3) an Applicant's reliance on that summary or conclusion. Those are not the same thing, and the ALJs should not treat reliance on a summary as though it were the underlying study itself. The supplemental proposal for decision should identify the record basis and evidentiary weight supporting any resulting reliability finding.
If the ALJs determine that the record should be reopened, Mr. Howton asks that any new evidence be limited to Issues 11 and 13, that all parties have a fair opportunity for discovery and cross-examination on it, and that any resulting substantial revision be set out in an amended or supplemental proposal for decision, as 16 TAC § 22.262(c)(2) provides.
V. CONCLUSION AND PRAYER
The remand asks two questions, and each has a record answer. Mr. Howton respectfully asks the ALJs to keep the proceeding within the scope of the Commission's remand and to answer each question with the specific standard, study, data, and analysis the record contains, or to state plainly where the record contains none.
For these reasons, Aaron Edward Howton respectfully requests that SOAH issue supplemental findings on Preliminary Order Issues 11 and 13 that identify, with record citations, the specific reliability standard, study result, underlying data, and analysis relied upon; that state where the record does not supply any of them; and that report, under PURA § 37.056(d), that the record contains no estimate of congestion cost savings for consumers.
Authorities cited: PURA § 37.056(a), (c-1), (d); 16 TAC §§ 22.261(c), 22.262(c), 22.263(a)(3), 25.101(b)(3)(A).
Respectfully submitted,
